speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. Agent, and I see you are here regarding a breast mass. To help me understand your condition, please tell me: when did you first notice this lump, and has its size changed since then? Also, is the mass painful or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: That rapid growth over just four weeks is concerning. Is the mass fixed to the skin or chest wall, or does it move freely? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the overlying skin, such as dimpling, redness, or an "orange peel" texture?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Fast-growing breast mass with no skin/nipple changes and no pain is most consistent with a phyllodes tumor (specifically a benign or borderline phyllodes tumor) rather than invasive carcinoma, which often presents with skin changes or fixation. I would like to confirm the mobility of the mass before proceeding. Is the mass mobile under the skin?
